title: install.sh orchestrator - machine, repo, and non-interactive flows
description: WHY: the install experience defines whether bwrk reads as a normal package; the flows must respect scope choice - a user who wants bwrk only inside one repo must get exactly that, with no PATH changes and no global prompts. CONTRACT (from the distribution epic brief): default flow installs or upgrades the machine binary, detects an existing global registry by file presence (never by guessing from PATH), prompts to set up the global addon only when absent, and offers to link the cwd repo when run inside one; the repo flow (--repo) adds the dev dependency to the current repo and verifies pnpm bwrk works, performing no PATH changes and never prompting about global - when a machine registry already exists it offers to link (--no-link to skip) and never creates global implicitly; the machine flow (--machine) installs the binary only and skips all global prompts; --global, --no-global, and --yes provide non-interactive overrides; re-runs are idempotent and the repo flow on an already-installed repo is an upgrade. WHAT: implement install.sh at the repo root against the dist artifact (sibling task) and the repo-scoped mode (sibling task); shellcheck-clean with a script-based test matrix covering fresh machine, existing global, repo-only with and without an existing registry, machine-only, and all non-interactive flags. NOTE: the bwrk global first-run bootstrap that was previously in this task moved to the global-manager epic (sprint G1) - do not implement it here.
acceptanceCriteria: Test matrix passes for default, repo, machine, and non-interactive flows with idempotent re-runs
The repo flow performs zero PATH or machine-level changes, verified by the test matrix
